mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 50,000 jobs and unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 4.5%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be positive due to stronger labor market confidence and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are not significantly above the mean of the prior 30-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102.0, accompanied by a rise in consumer demand proxy HOUST, predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the signal (Rank IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side index (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are more likely to be negative due to expectations of future contraction and tighter liquidity.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during the identified contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as lower inflation expectations reduce equity premium valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3.5% and retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeds 150,000 for a month, S&P 500 60-day forward returns tend to be positive due to heightened hiring optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the prior 30-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales proxy HOUST of over 200 units in a month coincides with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals demand softening and equity risk aversion rising.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by more than 200 units in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the shock period.

mechanism_narrative: When the supply index (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months, S&P 5-day forward returns are more likely to be positive as market participants anticipate a normalization in production constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO is flat for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative despite the supply flatness (p < 0.05).
